function: Classifies the optimal DM-RS allocation (1 of 13 NR patterns) for the next slot from uplink CSI, jointly with channel prediction, without CSI feedback (pp. 1-2).
system: Massive MIMO FDD OFDM downlink: BS 8x8 array, UE 2x1 array, no RIS; NR band n1 (UL 1.95 GHz, DL 2.14 GHz), 100 MHz bandwidth (p. 3).
method: ViViT (spatial and temporal transformer encoders) and 3D-CNN classifiers over 13 allocations, trained end to end with supervision on exhaustive-search labels (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Sionna ray tracing, scene simple_street_canyon_with_cars, UE at 60-80 km/h; Gaussian error (~0.05) added; 6,000 slots split 8:1:1 into train, validation, test (p. 3).
test_conditions: Same scene and speeds for training and test; held-out 10% split, 250 test slots; SNR swept -10 to 15 dB, training SNR not stated (pp. 3-4).
baselines: Learned: DRL (CNN-based DQN [24]), Disjoint ViViT/CNN predictor [22] plus pilot pruning [23]; non-learned: Maximize Data Symbols heuristic, Random Average; oracle Best (p. 4).
metrics: Allocation classification accuracy per SNR (Table II), average data throughput and gain over second-best benchmark (Fig. 4), NMSE of the disjoint channel predictor (pp. 4-5).
complexity: ViViT O(L(N^2 D + N D^2)); 3D-CNN O(L F C K^3 HWT); ViViT with L=8, N=64, D=128 needs about 1.082e9 FLOPs, about 3.47 us on A100 (p. 3).
q1_support: p. 3: "ray-tracing module of NVIDIA Sionna" and "We employed the simple_street_canyon_with_cars scene"; Sionna's public ray tracer and built-in scene, not 3GPP or DeepMIMO (reviewer to confirm).
q2_support: p. 3: "split into training/validation/test sets with an 8: 1: 1 ratio"; p. 4: "We evaluated each scheme over SNRs" from -10 to 15 dB. Held-out split and SNR sweep only; no new scene, band, array, or speed.
q3_support: p. 4: "DRL [24]: A CNN-based deep Q-network" (learned) and "Maximize Data Symbols: A heuristic scheme" plus "Random Average" (non-learned), compared on accuracy and throughput.
q4_support: p. 3: "The ViViT complexity is O(L(N 2 D + N D2 ))"; footnote 1 gives about 1.082e9 FLOPs ("the ViViT model requires") and about 3.47 us on an A100.
q5_support: p. 3: "yielding 6,000 slots in total"; the dataset is generated by the authors with Sionna ray tracing; no code or data link or DOI appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Borderline function: the learned classifier picks the DM-RS pattern from uplink CSI jointly with downlink channel prediction (abstract, p. 1; Sec. II, p. 2), counted as area 2; a reviewer could instead see link adaptation. Supervised paradigm inferred from classification on exhaustive-search labels (p. 3); the word is not used. q1: Sionna RT with its built-in public scene, marked met for confirmation. q5 is 0 because the generated channels and labels are not released. The check of the first page shows the title Standards-Compliant DM-RS Allocation via Temporal Channel Prediction for Massive MIMO Systems, matching the DOI.
